subject: Annual commit — bounded overage & smoothing options
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@orchidai.com>

Cc: Orchid AI Procurement <contracts@orchidai.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Annual commit and overage mechanics

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked solid and the latency numbers were compelling. We need to lock in an annual commit for our hosted usage, but procurement is pushing back on open-ended overage exposure. Two asks from our side:

1) Can you provide a clear three-tier commit structure (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) with per-token discounts and an explicit overage rate (per million tokens) we can accept without additional approvals?
2) We want an optional smoothing / crediting mechanism so we don’t get hit by a big spike mid-quarter. Ideally some kind of carry-forward credits or a buffer that reduces the overage rate for the first 20% over the commit.

Also, any onboarding or upfront credit you typically include for new enterprise customers? We’re aiming to finalize commercial terms by Aug 10.

Tom
Tom Li
VP, Platform & Infrastructure
Orchid AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Orchid AI Procurement <contracts@orchidai.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Annual commit and overage mechanics

Tom — really appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise proposal that should map to your procurement checklist; I’ve also attached a draft summary and the onboarding SOW workbook for numbers.

Summary (Starter / Growth / Enterprise):
- Starter: 250M tokens/year @ $0.0095 per 1k tokens (baseline) — 5% discount vs list; overage: $11.00 per million tokens.
- Growth: 1B tokens/year @ $0.0078 per 1k tokens — 20% discount vs list; overage: $9.00 per million tokens.
- Enterprise: 5B tokens/year @ $0.0060 per 1k tokens — 40% discount vs list; overage: $6.00 per million tokens.

Bounded overage / smoothing options (two choices):
A) Buffer band (recommended): first 20% over commit incurs a reduced overage at 50% of the standard overage rate (e.g., Growth: first 20% = $4.50/million, thereafter $9.00/million). This propagates in monthly billing and shows clearly on invoices.
B) Credit smoothing: we apply a 3-month rolling smoothing window. If a quarter exceeds the committed run rate, we pull from accumulated unused tokens from prior quarters up to 15% of annual commit; remaining usage billed at standard overage.

Onboarding / upfront credits: commonly offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) that covers up to $10k of consumption for Enterprise offers, and $2–5k for Growth/Starter depending on exec approval. We can make this a line item in the SOW.

Extras / operational controls:
- Burst capacity add-on for predictable spikes (charged as a monthly reservation).
- Auto-fallback policy to smaller model family if we hit capacity with a pre-agreed quality threshold (to avoid severe latency/regressions).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which smoothing option (A or B) procurement prefers.
2) Pick tier and target effective start date (we can pro-rate the first month).
3) I’ll issue a term sheet + DocuSign with the agreed tier, overage band, and onboarding credit line.

Attaching: redwood_commit_summary_draft_v1.pdf, SOW_onboarding_estimates.xlsx

Thanks — can hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
